name: Grosvenor Bridge (Chester)
facts: The Grosvenor Bridge, opened by a 13‑year‑old Princess Victoria on 17 October 1832, was the world’s longest single‑span stone arch bridge for 30 years, spanning 200 feet across the River Dee.

Designed by Thomas Harrison, the bridge’s 60‑foot high limestone arch was built on a drier downstream site after initial plans threatened softer ground, ensuring the structure could support its massive weight.
A toll of £50,000 funded construction, but after 50 years the fee was abolished in 1885, transferring maintenance to Chester Corporation and boosting trade across the city.
